title: Brindle Market search architecture
brief: I'm the tech lead for search at Brindle Market, an online marketplace for craft sellers, and I want an architecture page I can show on a laptop in the onboarding session for the six engineers joining on 2026-11-02. Begin with "How search works" in two sentences: sellers' listing changes appear in search within 60 seconds, and shoppers get results in under 300 milliseconds at the 95th percentile. Then "Component diagram" with these parts: Seller Portal, Listing Service, Change Stream, Indexer, Search Cluster, Query API, Ranking Service, Result Cache, Shopper App. Connections: Seller Portal to Listing Service "save listing"; Listing Service to Change Stream "listing changed"; Change Stream to Indexer "consume events"; Indexer to Search Cluster "update index"; Shopper App to Query API "search request"; Query API to Result Cache "check first"; Query API to Search Cluster "on cache miss"; Search Cluster to Ranking Service "top 200 candidates"; Ranking Service to Query API "re-ranked 24". Then "Sizing" as a table of component, count and note: Search Cluster, 9 nodes, 3 shards with 2 replicas each; Indexer, 4 workers, handles 900 events per second; Result Cache, 2 nodes, hit rate about 62 percent; Ranking Service, 6 instances, 40 millisecond budget. Last, "What to watch": index lag over 60 seconds, cache hit rate under 50 percent, and any shard with no healthy replica. Index lag is the alarm people forget, so highlight it.

edit.request: Add a node called "Spell Corrector" between Query API and Search Cluster, with the arrow from Query API labeled "fix typos", and grow the Search Cluster to 12 nodes with 4 shards.
